items.original: RES-EP13-18. A-9's hidden window is invisible to a region that reads bindings, and it is NOT invisible to a region that reads the ledger wrapper's own closure cell, nor to one that counts the ledger entries its own call produces The anchor's internal calls do not re-enter the shared ledger, and that difference is a side channel this instrument measures rather than denies: MD5 uses it and escapes The hidden window works by writing the contents of a closure cell that the ledger's own wrapper holds, which is a thing this guard can do and a region can observe if it looks there. It is also detectable without looking anywhere: an unobserved commitment call re-enters the ledger for its internal canonical call and an anchor-served one does not, so the entry delta says whether anyone is measuring. MD5 is that region, it is built and executed on every ordinary run, and it escapes every scored guard while routing every pinned commitment to the superseded encoder.
